changelog:
What you'll see with this update:
• Alert emails keep working on the newest Home Assistant versions. Home Assistant is retiring the built-in email feature this fleet used, so alert mail (SD card trouble, data-check problems, repeated restarts) is now sent by the Cytech software itself. What you receive, and who receives it, is unchanged, and the Send Test Email button still confirms a send only when the mail really went out.
• An old HTTP/proxy setting has been cleaned out of the configuration file, because Home Assistant has already moved it into its own settings. Home Assistant will refuse to start with it left in the old place from early 2027. Remote access is unaffected.
• The System Health screen now also checks the network port. If that port has no connection, the screen says so and tells you who to contact, and a new Check Network Port button re-checks it on demand. This update adds no new emails or pop-ups.
details:
v48 is the fleet-wide release of the two bench-only rounds 48a and 48b, confirmed ready and promoted together (nothing in either was reversed or superseded, so both appear below in full).

48b adds an Ethernet port check to the System Health screen, prompted by a real customer report: a new UCMA/Pi whose onboard port shows no link LEDs on any of several proven-good switches and cables, with NetworkManager refusing to activate end0 because the device has no carrier -- the owner was running on a USB NIC, and nothing on the unit told them the port was dead. A self test that names the fault on the owner's own screen is the point of this round; the fault itself ends in an RMA. New cytech_check_eth.sh is READ-ONLY on the network stack -- it reads /sys/class/net/* and nothing else, never runs ip link set or ethtool, and cannot change interface state. That is deliberate: this fleet has a history of scripts fighting NetworkManager over interface ownership (bounce_nic.py is the precedent and is deliberately not used here), and a link check has no business touching state. Interface resolution matches first_boot.sh's existing fallback (end0, else eth0). Three statuses: OK carries the real negotiated link speed read from sysfs; NO_LINK is the customer's case; NO_IFACE means neither name exists, which is a different, pre-existing fault. On NO_LINK the script scans the other interfaces for one that still has link and names it in owner-facing words (a USB network adapter for usb*/enx*, Wi-Fi for wl*), so a unit limping along on a USB NIC says exactly that. That scan requires the interface's device symlink to exist, because /sys/class/net reports carrier=1 for docker0, tailscale0, hassio, lo and every veth* pair -- without the filter the message would have read online via docker0 (verified live on the bench). ethtool is not installed on these units, so the check is pure sysfs, and the result is written with the same python3 JSON idiom the other check scripts use. Env overrides CY_ETH_DEV and CY_ETH_CARRIER are for offline testing only and are unset on-device; both are strictly read-only (one picks which interface is read, the other substitutes the value read -- never written), which is how the NO_LINK and NO_IFACE wording was exercised on the bench without unplugging anything. packages/cytech.yaml gains shell_command.cytech_check_eth, a command_line sensor (unique_id cytech_ethernet_result_sensor -> sensor.cytech_ethernet_result; the state is the short status word and all the prose lives in the message attribute, so HA's 255-char state cap never bites; scan_interval 5s, the hdmi/usb family's cadence, so the dashboard button visibly refreshes the row) and a new automation cytech_check_eth_health, triggered at every core start and every 4 hours. It is a new automation rather than an extra action on cytech_start_health_checks (start-only SD health -- a periodic trigger there would silently change the SD checks' cadence) or on cytech_check_config_health (config-integrity identity). dashboards/system.yaml adds a Network heading with the result line (green tick / warning triangle) and a Check Network Port button after the SD Card group; the section intro now names the network port too and says MOST problems also send an email, because this row deliberately does not: it is display-only by decision -- no new alert kind in cytech_alert_mail.py, no persistent notification, no popup. A dead Ethernet port on a unit that is otherwise online is exactly what the owner sees and reports themselves, and the alternative (an email every 4 hours from any unit whose cable is out) is worse. ALSO FOUND while building this, deliberately NOT fixed here: cytech_check_config_health uses a bare time_pattern hours: 4, which HA treats as an EQUALITY match, so it fires once a day at 04:00 rather than every 4 hours as its own comment claims; the new automation uses hours: "/4" (divisibility) instead. The config check's bare 4 is mitigated in practice by the v44 SSH-addon watcher re-running the integrity check every 5 minutes, and is left alone in 48b as a separate, one-character decision. Nothing else changed: no first_boot.sh, reset script, cytech_update.sh, secrets or other dashboard change, and no behaviour change for anything already working.

48a clears the two repairs an upgraded unit shows on HA's Repairs screen after HA 2026.9 imports two YAML blocks into its own storage: http/deprecated_yaml (the YAML block must be deleted -- leaving it is a startup FAILURE from HA 2027.2, not a warning) and homeassistant/deprecated_yaml_smtp (the legacy notify.smtp services stop working in HA 2027.3). Nothing was broken before this: both features still work on today's HA, and the two deadlines are months away. Two different fixes, because the two blocks are reachable in different ways.

(1) HTTP: new ensure_http_yaml_migrated() in first_boot.sh's maintenance pass removes the top-level http: block from /config/configuration.yaml. configuration.yaml can't be fixed by an update sync (cytech_update.sh deliberately never touches it -- an operator's hand edits and HA's own imports live there), so the edit has to be made on the device, at boot, like the v34 comfort-alarm value_template. The only gate is HA's own marker: data.yaml_migration_done in .storage/http, which HA sets once it has imported the block and .storage/http has become authoritative. That is per-device truth rather than a version guess -- at that moment the block is inert, so removing it cannot change how the device behaves, and a unit whose HA has not migrated yet (the 2026.6 fleet image) has no marker and is left completely alone. When such a unit's HA does migrate, its next boot removes the block -- no re-ship needed. The removal is proven four times over before it is allowed to trigger a restart: the file must currently parse (tolerant loader, !include tags and all); the slice being deleted must parse to exactly {'http': <the value the whole file parsed to>}, so a boundary that swallowed a neighbouring key aborts the edit; the edited text must parse and lose no other top-level key; and after the atomic replace the file is re-read and re-parsed, with the success line -- the only thing that triggers the restart -- printed only if the block is really gone. The last check is the important one: a pass that restarted without removing the block would restart again on every following pass, forever, and because this restart goes through restart_core_planned() the v45 planned-restart marker would exempt all of them and the Repeated Restarts detector would never notice. A one-shot configuration.yaml.pre_v48a_backup is kept on the device for recovery, and the v42 known-good snapshot is refreshed immediately after the edit so a later corruption restore cannot put the block back.

(2) SMTP/alerts: alert mail no longer goes through HA's smtp notify platforms at all. New cytech_alert_mail.py sends it with smtplib directly -- the same way cytech_register_email.sh has always sent the owner's registration confirmation -- so behaviour is identical on every HA version in the fleet and nothing has to be written into HA's own storage or config entries. packages/cytech.yaml's four alert automations and the Send Test Email button now call shell_command.cytech_alert_mail_<kind> (integrity/sdcard/canary/boot/test), one FIXED command per kind: the alert text is read by the script out of the same device-local result file HA's own command_line sensors read, so the wording, subjects and destinations are unchanged, and no alert text, template or owner input ever reaches a shell command line. Support@cytech.biz still gets every alert and the owner's registered address still gets its automatic copy when one is registered (the v41 rule, now enforced inside the script); Send Test Email goes to the owner alone. The command is deliberately INLINE, not detached like the fleet's other shell_commands: HA waits for its exit code, so a missing credential (plain-English 'email not configured') or a send that failed after two attempts aborts the caller and can never be reported as a success -- the v45b property, preserved. Exit codes: 0 sent, 1 bad usage, 2 not configured, 3 send failed. It logs one line per run to /config/cytech_alerts.log (never a credential), and its two-global budget of 2x20s fits inside HA's non-configurable 60s shell_command limit. cytech_email_gen.py now only deletes the leftover generated package -- which is what actually retires the two notify services and clears the repair -- keeping its one-status-line contract so both callers still know when a restart is needed. cytech_register_email.sh is deliberately unchanged, as is every dashboard.

(3) Deliberately NOT used anywhere in this: HA's supervisor API from inside the core container (its SUPERVISOR_TOKEN returns 401 there -- verified live 2026-09-15) and any write to HA's .storage/core.config_entries. Nothing here depends on an HA feature that the next upgrade can change.

v47 is the fleet-wide release of the bench-only 47a-47b feature revisions (both confirmed ready and promoted together; nothing in either was reversed or superseded, so both appear below in full).

47a adds a 'Latest first' toggle to the Alarm Message Log on the Comfort Alarm dashboard. New input_boolean.alarm_log_latest_first in packages/cytech.yaml -- a display preference only, with initial state deliberately left unset so a fresh unit comes up off (the pre-47a oldest-first order); nothing in the bridge or the log itself changes. dashboards/alarm.yaml puts the new toggle beside the existing Clear button in a two-column grid (Clear's fixed 48px width dropped so both fill the column), and the log markdown now splits sensor.comfort_mqtt_log's 'log' attribute on newlines and reverses the list while the toggle is on. Live-verified on cytech.local 2026-09-11: the shipped template rendered through HA's own /api/template against the real retained log -- toggle off reproduced the raw order exactly, toggle on the exact reverse.

47b adds a 'Dismiss Warning' button on the System Health dashboard. It's a conditional button card (dashboards/system.yaml, in the SD Card entities group right after the Warnings row) that only renders while sensor.cytech_warning is REPEATED_RESTARTS, and calls persistent_notification.dismiss on notification_id cytech_boot_alert -- the exact id the existing cytech_alert_boot_storm automation uses when it creates the 'Repeated restarts detected' popup. No new entities/helpers, so no restart is needed for it to take effect (YAML dashboards render current content on load). Scope note: this only dismisses the popup/banner -- sensor.cytech_warning itself, and the Warnings row's text, are unchanged by this button; that sensor only re-evaluates on the next HA Core start (see check_boot_storm() in first_boot.sh), so the row can keep reading REPEATED_RESTARTS for a stale reason after the popup is dismissed until the unit next restarts. Prompted by a live case on ems.local: 5 reboots recorded 2026-09-04 through 2026-09-08 (the Comfort panel's 24h battery test power-cycling the unit before a backup battery was connected), then none since -- but the notification and row stayed stuck on the 2026-09-08 snapshot for 3 days with no restart to re-trigger the check. Deployed and config-verified on ems.local 2026-09-11 (applied clean, button block present, no errors in the Core log); the button itself was not visually exercised there -- that deploy's own restart cleared the warning it was built to dismiss.

v46 is the fleet-wide release of the bench-only 46a fix revision, confirmed ready after cytech.local and ems.local both successfully applied it and correctly detected it as newer than their prior 45a/45b state.

v45 is the fleet-wide release of the bench-only 45a-45b fix revisions (both confirmed ready and promoted together; nothing in either was reversed or superseded, so both appear below in full).

v44 is the fleet-wide release of the bench-only 44a-44d fix revisions (previously staged as an aborted same-day 'v44' commit, immediately relabeled 44a since it wasn't ready for the fleet -- so this is the first time the plain '44' version/tag has actually shipped). What v44 ships:
(1) Config self-heal watcher now runs independently of HA Core: new ensure_config_integrity_watcher() in first_boot.sh (same pattern/de-dup approach as ensure_reset_watcher) runs cytech_integrity_check.py from inside the SSH addon container every 5 minutes, instead of only from a homeassistant.start-triggered automation. Fixes a real gap found by a live corruption test 2026-09-06: a configuration.yaml broken badly enough to fail parsing puts HA Core into Safe Mode, which does not load custom automations -- so the self-heal checker never ran in exactly the one case it exists for. Reproduced live (truncated configuration.yaml left the unit stuck in Safe Mode with no restore/alert/email); fixed and live-verified same day.
(2) Alert email moves from mail.server282.com (ucmapi@cytech.biz) to Gmail SMTP (cytechalerts@gmail.com). The old account was a single shared plaintext credential across the whole fleet with no per-device isolation or rotation path; Gmail App Passwords give each device its own revocable credential. cytech_email_gen.py's two notify platforms (cytech_alert_support, cytech_alert_email) now point at smtp.gmail.com, port 465/tls. Live-tested on the bench unit: both notify targets confirmed delivering, no SMTP/auth errors.
(3) New ensure_smtp_credential() in first_boot.sh distributes future SMTP credential rotations automatically: any device with CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN in .cytech_secrets fetches CY_SMTP_USER/CY_SMTP_PASS from a small private companion repo (ComfortHA-secrets, separate from this public one) via a read-only, single-repo, contents-only fine-grained PAT, and updates .cytech_secrets in place only if the values changed (idempotent -- a normal pass never restarts HA). Fetched from a private repo, not this one, because a public repo is scraped by credential-harvesting bots within minutes of a commit; if the fetch token itself leaks, the blast radius is limited to reading one small JSON file, not the SMTP password directly. Live-verified end-to-end on the bench unit.
CREDENTIAL CUTOVER, OPERATOR ACTION: the ucmapi@cytech.biz mailbox password is being rotated as part of this release, so it is no longer a working fallback for devices that haven't migrated. New devices get CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN baked in at provisioning and self-heal onto the new credential automatically. Already-fielded devices without the token will stop being able to send alert email until an operator adds CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN to that device's .cytech_secrets (over Remote Support Access or SSH) -- there is no bulk/automatic path for already-fielded units, so plan to migrate them opportunistically.
(4) 'Config Check' row shows just ok / restored / error / waiting -- no trailing epoch number.
(5) 'Boots' row renamed 'Warnings', with plain-English 'Repeated restarts' messaging (unchanged 5-restarts/24h guard).

v44 also carries everything v43 shipped (the fleet-wide release of the v42 series -- v42 plus fix-revisions 42a-42f, which only ever ran on the bench unit; 42a was an early rename-only attempt and 42d was a same-content re-ship for a delivery problem, so neither appears as a change below):
(1) CDN-proof downloads. raw.githubusercontent.com serves each URL from a CDN with max-age=300, keyed by the URL itself (a query string does NOT create a separate entry -- verified 2026-09-04), so a device downloading right after a release could be served the PREVIOUS version's file with no error, then write the new version label -- silently half-updated, and permanently unable to re-apply ('the units can never pull the real package, because the checker considers it up to date'). The bench unit hit exactly that during the 42c release. THE FIX: every release is git-tagged with its version and files are downloaded from the tag URL -- a URL no device has ever fetched, so it can never be served from cache. The manifest itself stays on the branch URL (stale reads there are harmless: 'up to date' for at most 5 minutes, then the next check is fresh). .cytech_secrets.example documents that CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL must not be pinned to a tag (the tag changes every release).
(2) cytech_integrity_check.py writes the status word only ('ok'), not 'ok <epoch>' -- the epoch leaked onto the Config Check dashboard row as an unexplained number.
(3) The boot guard state RESTART_STORM became REPEATED_RESTARTS with plain-English messages ('Repeated restarts detected' popup/email; message 'The unit restarted N times in the last 24h (first at HH:MM:SS local). Repeated restarts usually mean a problem -- please contact Cytech Support.'). Automation id cytech_alert_boot_storm is unchanged. (3b) The sensor 'Cytech Boot Status' is renamed 'Cytech Warning' -- the row is expected to carry other warnings besides boot/restart ones -- and its unique_id is bumped to cytech_warning_result_sensor on purpose: the entity registry pins an entity_id at first registration, so a name change alone would NOT move the id. A bumped unique_id re-registers every unit fresh as sensor.cytech_warning; units that already ran v35+ keep the orphaned sensor.cytech_boot_status (unreferenced, harmless). The on-disk result file (/config/.cytech_boot_result) and the dashboard row's message attribute are unchanged.
(4) The runtime integrity check also runs right after every core start (boot AND update restarts), not just every 4 hours, so the Config Check row shows its real result within minutes instead of 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart; before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'.
(5) Config self-healing: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts, and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, v44 also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.

45a adds two changes on top of 44:
(1) Bug fix: cytech_register_email.sh's owner-confirmation email (sent directly on a Register press, separate from the notify.smtp platforms cytech_email_gen.py generates) was still hardcoded to mail.server282.com with sender ucmapi@cytech.biz -- a leftover from before the 44b Gmail migration. Any device already running Gmail credentials (CY_SMTP_USER=cytechalerts@gmail.com, as cytech.local is) would fail this login and show the owner an error on every Register press, even with a correctly-spelled address. Reproduced live on the bench unit before fixing. Now uses smtp.gmail.com and sets the From header to whatever CY_SMTP_USER actually is (matches cytech_email_gen.py's notify platforms, and stays correct if the account is rotated again). Live-verified end-to-end on cytech.local 2026-09-07: Register press sent the confirmation, owner received it within seconds.
(2) New optional fleet registration log: a successful Register press also POSTs unit id, owner email, firmware version, and timestamp to a Google Sheet via an Apps Script web app, giving a running count/list of registered units across the fleet. Entirely best-effort and backward compatible -- gated on CY_SHEETS_WEBHOOK_URL + CY_SHEETS_SECRET both being present in .cytech_secrets (installer-seeded, same pattern as the SMTP credentials, never in this repo); a device without those two keys skips the POST entirely with zero network calls, and any failure (missing config, offline, endpoint error) is logged but never affects the owner-facing Register outcome. Live-verified end-to-end on cytech.local: the row for the 2026-09-07 registration test landed correctly (timestamp, unit cytech-3, owner email, firmware version 44d).
(3) Bug fix: 'Repeated restarts' (the Cytech Warning row) counted every HA Core restart identically, including the routine ones a normal Update Now pull or a Register press themselves cause -- so a day with several legitimate updates/registrations (or a support/testing session) could trip the false 'contact Cytech Support' warning with nothing actually wrong. Reproduced live on cytech.local: today's testing alone pushed it to 'restarted 12 times in the last 24h'. Fix: new restart_core_planned() in first_boot.sh marks a restart as planned (touches /config/.cytech_planned_restart) right before triggering it; record_boot_event() consumes that marker and skips recording the resulting restart, at all 9 known routine-restart call sites (first_boot.sh's dashboard/package/email/template maintenance fixes, cytech_update.sh's post-update restart, cytech_register_email.sh's post-register restart). Config self-heal restores are deliberately NOT routed through this -- repeated corruption is itself a real signal and should keep counting. Verified with an offline fixture (10 simulated planned restarts logged zero events, still OK; 5 genuine unplanned restarts still correctly tripped REPEATED_RESTARTS; a simulated self-heal restart still counted) and live end-to-end on cytech.local: cleared the false-positive backlog, then a real Register press confirmed logged 'Planned restart -- not counted' and the count stayed unchanged.

45b adds one more change on top of 45a:
(4) Bug fix: the 'Send Test Email' dashboard button called notify.cytech_alert_email directly with no feedback on success -- only a failure (e.g. 'action not found', the exact symptom hit live on ems.local when its SMTP credentials were still the pre-44b account) showed anything on screen, so a successful send looked identical to doing nothing. New script.cytech_send_test_email (packages/cytech.yaml) wraps the notify call and creates a persistent notification ('Test Email sent -- check your inbox') only on success; a failure still surfaces exactly as before (the script call itself errors out, nothing is silently reported as sent). dashboards/system.yaml's button now calls this script instead of the raw notify service. Live-deployed and config-verified error-free on both cytech.local and ems.local 2026-09-07.

Also same-day, found and fixed independently of this release's own code: ems.local (v45a) hit 'action notify.cytech_alert_email not found' on Send Test Email -- root cause was its .cytech_secrets still holding the pre-44b ucmapi@cytech.biz credential with no CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN to self-heal it, so cytech_email_gen.py's Gmail-only server assumption produced a package that could never authenticate and the notify service never registered. Fixed by adding the token (same private-repo fetch mechanism already live on cytech.local since 44d) -- not a 45a/45b code change, a per-device credential gap from the original 44b cutover.

46a fixes a real bug in ver_newer() (first_boot.sh, cytech_update.sh, cytech_check_only.sh) that surfaced live the moment v45 shipped: a device already on "45a" reported "45a is the latest version" and refused the real fleet "45" release. Root cause: ver_newer()'s same-base-number tie-break ("45" vs "45a", digits equal) fell back to comparing the leftover letter suffix, and the original rule treated ANY letter suffix as newer than no suffix at all -- correct for the old mid-series pattern (42a newer than 42b, etc.) but backwards for the current policy, where a bare release is the fleet PROMOTION of its own base number's letters (see feedback_no_letter_versions) and must always outrank them. Fixed: bare now always outranks a lettered version of the SAME base number, in both comparison directions; differing-base comparisons (43 vs 42z, 46 vs 45a) are unaffected -- they were already handled correctly by the integer branch before ever reaching this logic. Verified with an offline fixture covering every real scenario: 45>45a, 45b>45a, 45 not > 45 (equal), 43>42f, 46>45a -- all pass. Shipped as a letter (not straight to bare 46) so this device-version-comparison fix itself gets confirmed before becoming the next fleet baseline, per current policy -- but note any device stuck on 45a/45b will correctly detect 46a (or any 46.x) as newer regardless of the bug, since that comparison never reaches the broken same-base code path.
